lesson_title: The Fire That Wouldn't Go Out
hook_text: The police thought shooting would stop the Soweto students, but it did the opposite.
clip_script: 16 June 1976. Police open fire on students in Soweto. They think it's over. It's not. Next day, Alexandra rises. Then Kagiso, Tembisa, Pretoria. Universities burn. Funerals turn into marches. In August, it reaches Cape Town, and something new happens: coloured students march beside African students. We are all black, they say, because we're all oppressed. Students turn to their parents: stay home from work. In September, hundreds of thousands do, and factories stand empty. The government answers with bullets and jail cells. Leaders are hunted and flee the country. By early 1977, an official inquiry counts 575 dead. Many believe it was more. But the fire never really went out. It was still burning, years later, when apartheid finally began to fall.
visual_style: A map of South Africa with points lighting up from Soweto outwards; students marching in Cape Town; an empty factory floor; police vans; a funeral crowd; a long list of names on a memorial wall.
mood: Urgent and tense, ending on quiet determination.
pacing: Fast as the protests spread, slowing for the stay-aways and the death toll.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to see how the uprising spiralled across South Africa.
